A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ATTNPO. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C are readable and can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original attention-head probing, model training, benchmark evaluations, ablations, and timing analyses in Sections 3 and 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original probing, training, evaluation, ablation, and timing results, including the supplementary empirical evidence.

M1.justification: KFH selection and scoring, outcome-level rewards, and the two stepwise advantage-attenuation strategies are unchanged. Section 4 and the step-segmentation algorithm in Appendix A.1 retain the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use DeepScaleR for training and probing, the same six mathematics benchmarks, and LiveCodeBench-v6, GPQA-Diamond, and MMLU for held-out evaluation. Newly cited datasets do not introduce evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the main tables, ablations, and supplementary analyses is unchanged. SHAPE, SPAE, and ROSE are newly discussed in Section 6 but are not added to the reported experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix B retain the same model sizes, benchmark subsets, metrics, training settings, and evaluation procedures, including 1,200 training steps, a 16K evaluation context, and temperature 0.6.

E4.justification: The head interventions, component and hyperparameter ablations, exploration and token-budget analyses, behavioral analysis, timing comparison, and case studies are unchanged in Sections 3 and 5 and Appendices A-C.

E5.justification: Both retain the same evaluation sampling counts, 16-sample training-dynamics evaluations, and inter-annotator agreement reporting. No seed information, uncertainty intervals, or significance-testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted trends, and case-study outputs match throughout. For example, Table 1 retains ATTNPO's macro-average accuracy/token counts of 61.8/3114 for 1.5B and 73.1/2922 for 7B.

T1.justification: The step-score and SRA definitions, optimization and rescaling equations, and appendix metric formulas are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, proof, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about discovering KFHs, providing low-overhead process supervision, and reducing reasoning length while improving accuracy across nine benchmarks.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the probing, ablations, exploration, and generalization results are retained. The limitations remain evaluation on 1.5B/7B models and mathematics-only training; the expanded literature discussion does not revise these interpretations or boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in a first-page footnote. Implementation details, selected heads, hyperparameters, hardware, and annotation instructions remain unchanged. The PDFs establish the added access information, not the repository's contents or accessibility.

R1.justification: Section 6 substantially broadens its coverage beyond outcome- and process-supervised RL to concise-data SFT/DPO, latent compression, dynamic reasoning selection, and inference-time interventions. It adds SHAPE, SPAE, ROSE, and discussion of entropy/confidence-based advantage shaping and its stated limitations, alongside numerous new references.

P1.justification: v2 expands and partly rewrites Section 6, makes small wording and citation edits elsewhere, changes author order, and adds acknowledgments. The main section sequence, method exposition, and appendix organization remain stable.

P2.justification: The added footnote, expanded related work, acknowledgments, and references cause local column and page reflow. Figures 1-15 and Tables 1-7 retain their displays; appendix page bodies match exactly after excluding page numbers.

improvement.justification: The expanded Section 6 provides broader research context, and the new code link improves access information. These offer limited overall gains while the scientific method, empirical evidence, and acknowledged limitations remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether the linked code is complete or usable.
